issues.title: P22B yield printed 4.09 t/ha, should be 4.98
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 18 prints P22B 518.58 t on 104.08 ha as 4.09 t/ha; 518.58 ÷ 104.08 = 4.98 t/ha, which Agro 2/2026 Table 14 prints. Dashboard uses 4.98.

issues.title: Manuring progress: PA 64% vs Agro 76%
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 10: 258.65 t applied of 406.70 t required (64%) to Jul 2026, of which Mix B 177.40 t, RP 70.95 t, kieserite 10.30 t. Agro 2/2026 Table 4 (mature, as of Jul 2026): 311.45 of 408.85 t (76%) with Mix B 212.90 t and RP 88.25 t; immature Table 5: 74.70 of 204.15 t (37%).

issues.title: PA manuring table total does not add
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 10 required column rows add to 458.20 t, but the printed total is 406.70 t (delivered 276.45 and applied 258.65 do add). 64% is 258.65 ÷ 406.70.

issues.title: Circle spraying total typo
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 7 total actual is printed 426.46 ha but the rows (167.64 + 208.16 + 86.66) add to 462.46 ha. kpi circlePct 59 = 462.46 ÷ 777.51 ha to-date budget (worked out); selectivePct 73 = 462.46 ÷ 630.10 (worked out). No estate pruning % printed.

issues.title: Fertiliser programme in PA vs Agro
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 10 schedules RP in April and June and Mix B in July, August and October for the mature area, broadly matching the Agro 1/2026 programme (P18C RP Apr; P22B/P22D RP Jun, Mix B Jul and Oct), but the PA lists kieserite in March only (10.30 t) and Mix B in January and February, which match P22 (Jan) and P18C (Feb).

issues.title: Weeding budget figure in text
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 6.1.6 says weeding RM129.46/ha is 28% below a to-date budget of RM260.00/ha; Table 6 shows the to-date budget as RM178.99/ha (RM260.00 was the 2025 annual budget). The 28% matches 178.99.

issues.title: General charges: two different totals
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 5 general charges to Jul 2026 RM374,905.27 (RM831.28/ha, budget RM539,609.00), but Table 20 cost of production uses RM225,880.00 (RM115.36/t, budget RM325,087.00). The ratio is about 60%, close to the mature share of planted area, but the report does not say how it is split.

issues.title: Yield vs last year on different areas
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 says 7.21 t/ha is 47% below the same period last year (13.63 t/ha). The 2025 figure is P18C only (167.64 ha, 2,285.14 t); 2026 is P18C + P22B (271.72 ha, 1,958.06 t). Tonnage fell 14%, not 47%.

issues.title: Barn owl box counts differ
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 13: P18C 14, P22B 10, P22D 18 = 42 boxes, 39 occupied (95%), while text 6.3.3 says 100% occupancy. Agro 2/2026 Table 12: P18C 14, P22B 10, P22D 4, P23A 18 = 46 boxes, 44 occupied (96%). The PA appears to place P23A's 18 boxes under P22D.

issues.title: Rat bait type differs
issues.detail: PA 2/2026: 1 round with STORM flocoumafen 0.005% over 315.05 ha. Agro 2/2026: first round with brodifacoum 0.005% after the March census.

issues.title: P23A palm density and compound type
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 13.2 says latest census 139 palms/ha for P23A; PA Table 1 and Agro 2/2026 Table 2 give 148/ha (25,556 palms). Agro Table 2 prints the P23A current count as 25,556, while Agro 1/2026 gave 26,616. P22D 122/ha (PA) vs 121/ha (Agro). PA 13.4 says 'Comp 44' applied; Agro Table 5 calls it 'Compound 25' (74.70 t).

issues.title: Agro immature table lists Mixture B
issues.detail: Agro 2/2026 Table 5 shows 79.60 t Mixture B required for immature plantings in 2026 (none received), but the 2026 programme for PR23A in Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1(b) has only compound and RP.

issues.title: P22B cost to maturity two figures
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 summary table says RM14,360.60/ha; section 13.1.10 says RM14,316.60/ha.

issues.title: Repeated and mislabelled text
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 14.9 repeats the 2025 road figures (2,386 chains graded, 783 mt crusher run) from PA 1/2026. The comment table in PA 2/2026 is headed 'P. A Report 1/2026'. Agro 2/2026 4.2.2 refers to 'P22C' (no such field; table shows P22B and P22D). Agro 2/2026 Table 16 gives P23A as 179.24 ha (179.28 elsewhere). PA 2/2026 Appendix 2 'Other expenditures' sub-total RM3,651.75 with cost/ha RM3,437.85 does not reconcile (MSPO and ISCC lines cancel out).

issues.title: Traps checked
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Table 17 '2025 same period' (2,285.14 t) is real Jan–Jul 2025 actual and '12 months' (4,651.78 t) is a genuine full year; no Jan–Nov totals; no combined estates. P22D (tapping right) is excluded from the estate t/ha but included in Table 16/18 totals (2,049.70 t).

LADANG CEMPAKA (Far East Holdings Berhad) - PARAS report fact pack

REPORTS USED
- Planting Advisory (PA) Report 2/2026: visit 27 August 2026, period reviewed January to July 2026. Planting Advisor Tn. Hj. Mohd Sufian bin Yusoff. Estate Manager En. Muhammad Uzairi bin Abdul Rahim. Deputy COO / Plantation Controller En. Nazaruddin bin Hashim.
- PA Report 1/2026: visit 18 February 2026, reviewing January to December 2025.
- Agronomy Report 2/2026: visit 2 September 2026 (previous visit 19 January 2026), by En. Muhammad Nurhafizi bin Zahari (Junior Agronomist), checked by Mr. Chong Kuan Ming (Senior Agronomist). Contains the 2027 fertiliser programme.
- Agronomy Report 1/2026: visit 19 January 2026 by En. Ghazali bin Abdul Ghani. Contains the 2026 fertiliser programme (no amendment from Agro 2/2025).
- Agronomy Reports 1/2025 (visit 23 January 2025) and 2/2025 (visit 24 July 2025) used for history and the 2025 programme.

AREA (PA 2/2026 Table 1, July 2026)
Total 495.93 ha; planted 494.33 ha (143 palms/ha). Mature 315.05 ha: P18C 167.64 ha (planted 2018, Felda Yangambi, 140 SPH), P22B 104.08 ha (2022, Chemara DxP, 148 SPH), P22D 43.33 ha tapping-right land (2022, Chemara DxP, 122 SPH). Immature P23A 179.28 ha (2023, 148 SPH). Line site 1.60 ha. P22B and P22D declared mature January 2026; P23A started scout harvesting January 2026. Age profile 64% young mature, 36% immature. Flat to gently rolling, hilly along the Southern Keratong Plantations boundary. Five-year average rainfall about 2,100 mm over 115 days, peak November to January. Sub-blocks (Agro): P18C C1 52.55, C2 55.85, C3 59.24 ha; P22B B1 48.70, B2 55.38 ha; P22D D1 43.33 ha; P23A A1 62.28, A2 48.30, A3 68.70 ha.
Palm census by drone, first half 2026 (Agro 2/2026 Table 2): P18C 23,430 palms (140/ha, -2%); P22B 15,379 (148/ha); P22D 5,254 (121/ha, -22% from 148); P23A 25,556 (148/ha); estate 69,619 palms, 141/ha. P22D count to be reconfirmed; VOP canopy blocks drone counting in some areas. 80 palms supplied in P23A in June 2026.

CROP PRODUCTION (PA 2/2026 Table 17, Jan-Jul 2026)
FFB 1,958.06 t vs to-date budget 2,590.00 t (24% below); annual budget 5,300.00 t. Same period 2025: 2,285.14 t. Full year 2025: 4,651.78 t. Yield 7.21 t/ha (budget 9.53; Jan-Jul 2025 13.63; 2025 full year 27.75). The t/ha excludes tapping-right P22D. CPO 368.76 t at 18.83% OER; kernel 90.23 t at 4.61% KER. The PA says production was 47% below the same period last year in t/ha; note the 2025 figure covered P18C only.
By field Jan-Jul 2026 (PA Table 18): P18C 1,439.48 t, 8.59 t/ha, 5.46 bunches/palm, 11.23 kg bunch weight; P22B 518.58 t (printed 4.09 t/ha; Agro gives 4.98), 9.32 bunches/palm, 3.61 kg; P22D 91.64 t, 2.11 t/ha, 4.67 bunches/palm, 3.71 kg; total incl. P22D 2,049.70 t, 6.50 t/ha. P22D yield low due to low stand and many unproductive supply palms. P23A scout harvest 166.20 t in 7 months.
Agro 2/2026 Table 14 (to July): P18C 8.59 vs 13.63 t/ha in 2025 (-37%); P22B 4.98 vs 2.30 (+117%); P22D 2.11 vs 0.96 (+120%). P23A 0.93 t/ha vs estimate 1.39. Agronomist: P18C decline due to seasonal and crop factors, not upkeep or harvesting; promising bunch formation, higher second half expected. 14 harvesting rounds done in all fields (100%).
Full years (Agro monthly tables, P18C only): 2021 945.47 t; 2022 2,548.17 t (15.20 t/ha); 2023 3,251.77 t (19.40); 2024 3,472.73 t (20.72); 2025 4,651.78 t (27.75, +33.9%). 2025 scout harvesting P22B and P22D: 441.56 t, 3.00 t/ha vs 3.65 estimate (B1 2.82, B2 4.13, D 1.74 t/ha).
Monthly 2026 (t): Jan 289.96, Feb 252.50, Mar 219.24, Apr 175.20, May 207.30, Jun 305.44, Jul 508.52. Monthly 2025: Jan 307.34, Feb 209.34, Mar 295.70, Apr 314.46, May 267.46, Jun 366.24, Jul 524.60, Aug 554.84, Sep 491.14, Oct 486.12, Nov 454.60, Dec 379.94.

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA 2/2026 Table 20, Jan-Jul 2026, RM per t FFB)
General charges 115.36 (budget 125.52); upkeep and cultivation 177.14 (169.27); harvesting and collection 104.57 (131.32); total ex-estate 397.07 (426.11), 7% below budget; annual budget 356.95. RM totals: 777,494.00 vs 1,103,613.00 budget.
Harvesting and collection (Table 15): harvesting RM147,073 = RM75.11/t (budget 96.45); internal transport RM57,689 = RM29.46/t (34.86).
Upkeep RM/ha to date (Table 6): weeding 129.46 (budget 178.99), manuring 979.91 (996.54), pests and diseases 25.78 (120.82), census and thinning 3.15 (6.39), drains 61.64 (60.57), roads and bridges 29.86 (174.69), supplying 0.24, boundaries 4.62 (17.11), pruning 41.86 (58.35); total RM1,276.51/ha vs RM1,613.46.
General charges (Table 5): RM374,905.27 = RM831.28/ha, 14% below to-date budget RM1,196.47/ha. Overspent items: SOCSO management (HRDF levy), medical/VMO labour (+416%, ordinary rate of pay for sick pay), MSPO (+15%), ISCC (+8%).
2025 (PA 1/2026): cost RM245.49/t vs RM315.89 budget (22% below): general charges 57.08, upkeep 86.78, harvesting 101.64; grand total incl. processing, windfall tax and depreciation RM382.89/t. 2025 FFB 4,651.78 t was 22% above the 3,800 t budget.
Capital expenditure 2026: bearer plant RM3,077,545.05; one HP Pro computer RM5,420.00 (June 2026, unbudgeted). P23A cost to maturity RM10,955.19/ha excl. general charges. P22B cost to maturity RM14,316.60/ha.

LABOUR AND STAFF (PA 2/2026 Table 3, July 2026)
31 workers vs 32 required (1 worker per 16 ha, slightly short for upkeep): harvesters 18 of 18 (1 per 18 ha); driver/loader 1 of 2; weeding 3 of 4; manuring 5 of 4; mandor 2 of 2; general 2 of 2. 10 checkroll, 21 contract. Contractors: Ayden Smart (harvesting and weeding, 315.05 ha, 20 workers), Alam Shag (FFB transport). In 7 months: 4 recruited, 7 returned, 1 transferred in; 2 repatriated, 3 on long leave, 1 transferred out. Staff: Manager Muhammad Uzairi, Assistant Manager Muhammad Amir Asyraaf (from January 2026), Field Conductor Maizaitol Akmal, Account Clerk Aminuddin bin Arip.
Dec 2025 (PA 1/2026): 25 workers vs 34 required.

HARVESTING (PA 2/2026 section 7, 9)
Average interval 15 days, 14 rounds in 7 months; no ripe bunches left; all loose fruit collected; keep minimum ripeness of 1 detached loose fruit. Harvester output: P18C 1.80 t/man-day (RM54.00/t, RM97.20/day); P22B 0.91 (RM92.00/t, RM83.72/day); P22D 0.76 (RM92.00/t, RM69.92/day); estate 1.38 t/man-day from 1,487 man-days. Director target over 3.0 t/man-day. One Timac with 7 harvesters: 11.77 t/machine-day, 1.74 t/harvester-day. Consider another Timac. Agro: intervals 14-17 days Jan-Jul 2026, no over-ripe bunches.

MANURING
PA 2/2026 Table 10 to July 2026: Jan Mix B 36.15 t (100%); Feb Mix B 52.80 (100%); Mar Kieserite 10.30 (100%), Mix B 36.15 (100%); Apr RP 46.95 (100%); May Mix B 52.80, 52.30 applied (99%); Jun RP 41.30, 24.00 applied (58%); Jul Mix B 36.15, Aug Mix B 52.80, Oct Mix B 92.80 to come. Total 406.70 t required, 276.45 delivered, 258.65 applied (64%). Slight delay from delivery problems; follow up with the supplier. Worker output 24 bags/day at 1.50 kg and 30 bags/day at 2.00 kg, RM72.00/day.
Agro 2/2026 Table 4 (mature, to July): Mixture B 212.90 of 310.30 t (69%); Kieserite 10.30 (100%); RP 88.25 (100%); total 311.45 of 408.85 t (76%). Table 5 (immature): Compound 74.70 t (100%); Mixture B 79.60 t not received (0%); RP 49.85 t received, 0 applied; total 74.70 of 204.15 t (37%). Agronomist: delays should not exceed two months; finish outstanding June programmes by August.
2025: mature 258.20 t and immature 348.60 t, both 100%, finished November.

2026 FERTILISER PROGRAMME (Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1, grams per palm)
P18C: Feb Mix B 2250, Apr RP 2000, May Mix B 2250, Aug Mix B 2250, Oct Mix B 2250.
P22B: Jan Mix B 1750, Mar Kieserite 500, Apr Mix B 1750, Jun RP 2000, Jul Mix B 1750, Oct Mix B 2000.
P22D: Jan Mix B 1750, Mar Kieserite 500, Apr Mix B 1750, Jun RP 2000, Jul Mix B 1750, Oct Mix B 1750.
P23A: Feb Compound 1500, May Compound 1500, Jun RP 2000, Aug Compound 1500, Nov Compound 1500.
2027 programme (Agro 2/2026 Appendix 1): P18C Feb Mix B 2250, Mar Kieserite 750, May Mix B 2250, Jul RP 2000, Aug Mix B 2250, Oct Mix B 2250. P22B and P22D Jan Mix B 2000, Mar Kieserite 500, Apr Mix B 2000, Jun RP 2000, Jul Mix B 2000, Oct Mix B 2000. P23A Feb Mix B 1750, Mar Kieserite 500, May Mix B 1750, Jun RP 2000, Aug Mix B 1750, Nov Mix B 1750. Mix B = 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate.
2025 programme (Agro 1/2025): P18C Feb Mix B 2000, Mar Kieserite 500, May Mix B 2000, Jul RP 2000, Aug Mix B 2250, Nov Mix B 2250; P22B and P22D Jan Mix B 1500, Feb Kieserite 500, Apr Mix B 1500, Jun RP 2000, Jul Mix B 1500, Oct Mix B 1500; P23A Jan Compound 1000, Apr Compound 1000, Jun RP 1750, Jul Compound 1200, Oct Compound 1200.

LEAF NUTRIENTS (Agro 2/2026 Table 7, sampled March 2026)
N high everywhere (2.87-3.18%). P normal to high. K high (1.24-1.64%). Mg: C1 0.29 H, C2 0.28 N, C3 0.26 N, B1 0.30 ML, B2 0.29 L, D1 0.30 ML. Ca: C1 0.61 H, C2 0.60 N, C3 0.47 ML, B1 0.39 L, B2 0.49 ML, D1 0.45 ML. B 12.82-16.88 ppm. Extra kieserite in 2027 for low Mg; Ca to be rechecked. Mg deficiency symptoms in some palms, not widespread.

WEEDING
PA 2/2026: circle spraying P18C 1 round, P22B and P22D 2 rounds each (rows 462.46 ha vs to-date budget 777.51 ha; table total printed 426.46). Selective spraying 462.46 ha vs 630.10 ha budget. Overspraying common, bare ground in P18C; restrict circle to 2 m radius; encourage soft grasses and Nephrolepis; spot spray wild seedlings with sodium chlorate herbicide. Sprayers: circle 5.00 ha/day RM80.00/day; selective 4.50 ha/day RM72.00/day.
Agro 2/2026: inter-row conditions acceptable; VOPs in P22B1 and P22B2; Clidemia hirta patches in P18C1 and P18C2 not fully killed; weeding behind schedule especially P18C. Selective rounds: P18C 1, P22B 2, P22D 2. Circle rounds: P18C 1, P22B 2, P22D 2. P23A: 3 selective rounds done, circle 1st round 100%, 2nd round 54%, VOP eradication with circle rounds.

PESTS AND DISEASES
Rats (Agro 2/2026 Table 11): March 2026 P18C 15%, P22B 14%, P22D 14%; after baiting (April) 8%, 5%, 6%; August 18%, 16%, 16% - above the 10% threshold; immediate targeted baiting and follow-up census one month later. PA: 1 round of STORM flocoumafen 0.005% over 315.05 ha (Agro names brodifacoum). Barn owls: Agro 46 boxes, 44 occupied (96%); add boxes to 1 per 8 ha. PA 42 boxes, 39 occupied. No bagworm. Fallen palms suspected of Ganoderma referred to the Agronomist; de-bole promptly. P23A: bagworm, rhinoceros beetle and Apogonia under control; 1 round of carbosulfan 5% at 15 g/palm. Beneficial plants Cassia cobanensis, Antigonon leptopus, Turnera subulata 60:20:20.

PRUNING
Agro 2/2026 Table 8: P18C 1,173.48 of 2,011.68 ha (58%); P22B 104.08 of 208.16 (50%); P22D 43.33 of 86.66 (50%); on schedule. Over-pruning in P18C3 (harvester discipline) and in P23A. Keep at least 2 fronds below the lowest bunch in mature palms; in immature palms prune only when lowest bunch is 3 ft above ground. PA: standard satisfactory; frond restacking needs improvement.

DRAINS, ROADS, BOUNDARY
Drains Jan-Jul 2026: 219.08 chains 5x4x3 ft and 140.85 chains 8x6x4 ft desilted = 359.93 of 650.00 chains (55%), P18C and P22B low-lying areas. Roads: grading in progress, target August 2026; silt pits and scupper drains to be added; laterite soggy and steep stretches; frond tipping along roads. Boundary with Felda Bera cluster and Southern Keratong in good condition, regular patrols, no FFB left overnight. Gensets 82 and 83 RM15.37 and RM14.63 per hour (budget 14.40), higher diesel price.

RAINFALL (PA 2/2026 Appendix 1)
2026 Jan-Jul 936.0 mm in 48 days. 2025 2,089.5 mm/112 days; 2024 2,075.5/102; 2023 2,498.0/111; 2022 2,002.0/154; 2021 1,947/113. July 2025 had no rain.

KEY CONCERNS
1. Yield to July 2026 24% below budget; P18C down 37% on last year.
2. Rat damage above threshold again in August 2026.
3. Manuring delayed by fertiliser deliveries; P23A RP not applied; Mixture B balance not received.
4. VOPs in P22B, P22D and P23A; weeding behind schedule.
5. Over-pruning in P18C3 and P23A; low harvester output in new fields.
